meta.title: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2) GameData reference
meta.howToRead: Every key the game keeps in its GameData store is a 32-bit Murmur3 hash of its name (see hashing). keys: what we know per key; keys64: 64-bit placed-object flags; grants: the exact writes that give an item or value; checklistRecipes: per kind of checklist entry, the keys a real pickup sets; enums: value names for Enum/String64 keys; areas: stage ids with readable names. confidence: confirmed = seen in game or in a save diff at the right moment; likely = name and saves agree, not checked in game; guess = indirect, needs a diff.

hashing.encoding: UTF-8 bytes of the full key name, no terminator
hashing.output: u32, written as 0x + 8 upper-case hex digits
hashing.alsoUsedFor: Enum values: an Enum record holds murmur3(value name).
hashing.bool64bitKey: Placed-object flags (Skulltulas, some heart pieces, chests) use 64-bit keys that are not a hash of a known name; they are listed raw in keys64. Some objects keep a second key for the other age (key xor 2, unverified).

saveFormat.files: progress.sav (per slot; caption.sav, option.sav, account.sav use the same container)

header.field: start of the data area (end of the record table)

saveFormat.records: From 0x28 to the data area: 8-byte records {u32 key hash, u32 value}. A record with hash 0 starts a section; its value is the type id of the records that follow. The first section (Bool) has no separator.
saveFormat.inlineNote: Inline types keep the value in the record (Bool: non-zero = true; Enum: murmur3 of the value name). Every other type stores an offset into the data area; offsets ascend and each value ends where the next begins.

encodings.BoolArray: u32 bit count, then bits packed in u32 words (bit i = word i>>5, bit i&31)
encodings.Bool64bitKey: one record; its offset points to an ascending list of u64 keys running to the end of the file. Only keys that are set are stored; offset 0 = none; a trailing 0 is padding.

liveMemory.readOnlyNote: The live tables are a copy of the same GameData store (saves are written from it). Trust them only after they agree with the latest save. Records can move: re-check the vtable before every access.

games.memory: guest address G is at host 0x100000000000 + G
placed somewhere new every run: sweep MEM_MAPPED regions (VirtualQueryEx) for the tables

tables.note: three 64-byte text buffers, each after a pointer + capacity; the one at +0x74 is the current value

liveMemory.vtable: Every record of a table starts with the same 8-byte pointer (the type's vtable). It is read at run time from the table itself, not hard-coded.
liveMemory.hashMap: Directly before each record array: a hash map of {u32 key hash, u32 record index}. Resolve a key through it; never guess an address.

bool64Table.layout: u64 key at +0x0, class byte at +0x8 (0x18 permanent, 0x58 respawning), set byte at 0x0000000C (1 = set)

liveMemory.locating: Scan readable memory (around the guest base, or every MEM_MAPPED region for emulators) for runs of records that share one 8-byte pointer at the type's stride, at least minRecords long. Read the hash map before the run and compare the values with the latest save; keep the best-scoring run per type. Use the tables only while they still match the save (≥90% of the save's true flags still true).

engineObjects.layout: u64 vtable at +0x0, i32 value at 0x00000008, u32 murmur3(key) at 0x0000000C
engineObjects.note: Some values (current hearts) really live here; the store record is a per-frame copy. PlayerStatus.Life is directly followed by PlayerStatus.MaxLife with the same vtable. Address changes every run; find by key hash and re-check vtable + hash before each access.

liveMemory.writing: To change a value: key hash → hash map → record → check vtable → write every copy → read back. Possession flags do not equip wearables or grant their abilities by themselves.

keys.name: AskBonooru_listentothesong
keys.evidence: UNCONFIRMED / ON HOLD (2026-11-18): the flag field below is the WRONG songbook key - do not trust it. Save-diff on a legitimate learn (slot_05, 2026-11-17): AskBonooru_listentothesong (0xFDF0F4B8) flipped false→true; note array 0xCC535536 (UIntArray[8]) populated (button values A=11, Y=13, X=16, L=4, R=7; the real learn used [4,4,7,7,4,4,7,7]); timing blob 0x3339DF55 (Binary, 376 bytes) created. In game (2026-11-17): the songbook flag is IsGet.Item_Melody_ScarecrowSong (0x5E86FB4D) — setting it put the song in the songbook immediately, and every other learned song in the save has IsGet.Item_Melody_<song> = true; AskBonooru_listentothesong is only a Bonooru conversation step (with it on, saved, plus the notes, the song was NOT in the songbook). So the flag field (currently AskBonooru) is the wrong key — left as-is while the Scarecrow fix is on hold. The save-file note write is likely [pending: in-game]: a notes + timing-blob write loads cleanly in game (only 2 of 11,925 keys changed); the blob is a resize write (+376 bytes) the trainer's same-size-only writer doesn't do yet, so the trainer writes the notes only. Full grant unconfirmed: playing the song as a child (IsGet on) froze the game (process exited, nothing saved) — cause unknown (progress values like Step_SubEvent_GetScarecrow not advanced, or the child path is unhandled — in the original only adults use it); adult play untested.
